summary: Ishan Anand's talk uses a full Excel implementation of GPT-2 small as a teaching tool for engineers without machine learning backgrounds. The spreadsheet contains over 150 tabs and 124 million cells corresponding to GPT-2 small's parameters, using only pure Excel functions. The talk is structured as a medical analogy: studying the patient's anatomy, performing a virtual MRI, and conducting brain surgery. The anatomy section covers the full forward pass: input text is split into subword tokens, mapped to 768-dimensional embeddings, processed through 12 layers of attention and multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs), and then the language head reverses the embedding process to produce a probability distribution over possible next tokens. Tokenization is shown to not always match human intuition (e.g., 'reinjury' splits into 'rain' and 'jury'). Attention lets tokens look backward at previous tokens for context, with causal masking preventing forward looks. Residual connections act as an information superhighway, letting information skip layers. The virtual MRI section uses the logit lens technique, inserting the language head between layers to observe what the model predicts at each stage. For the prompt 'If today is Tuesday tomorrow is,' Wednesday appears early then disappears, reemerging in later layers. Researchers found only four components needed for correct day-of-week prediction: perceptron layer 0, one attention head in layer 9, perceptron layer 9, and attention layer 10, illustrating how layers form circuits to accomplish tasks. The brain surgery section covers Anthropic's work on scaling monosemanticity, which produced Golden Gate Claude, a model obsessed with the Golden Gate Bridge. Sparse autoencoders decompose the residual stream into interpretable features that can be amplified or suppressed by injecting steering vectors. Joseph Bloom, Neel Nanda, and others are building sparse autoencoder features for GPT-2 small; layer 2's feature 7650 corresponds to 'Jedi.' Anand demonstrates injecting this Jedi steering vector into the residual stream, changing GPT-2's output from 'Mike pulls out his phone' to 'Mike pulls out his lightsaber.' He also mentions representation engineering (PCA-based) and activation steering (concept-minus-suppress vector) as alternative techniques. The talk concludes that understanding LLM internals helps engineers use models better, follow research, and communicate with non-technical stakeholders, noting that model architecture even affects prompting patterns, as RWKV recommends swapping instruction and context order due to its attention limitations.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction and Overview
sections.summary: Anand introduces himself and the medical analogy: attendees are AI brain surgeons, GPT-2 is the patient, and an Excel spreadsheet is the operating table. The spreadsheet implements all of GPT-2 small in pure Excel functions with 150+ tabs and 124+ million cells. The talk has three parts: anatomy, virtual MRI, and brain surgery.

sections.title: Anatomy: Converting Word Problems to Math Problems
sections.summary: Explains that LLMs are trained to complete sentences. The approach converts a word problem into a math problem: text is broken into tokens, mapped to embeddings (many numbers each), processed through attention and MLP, and the result is interpreted as a probability distribution for the next token. A chart maps each step to spreadsheet tabs.

sections.title: Tokenization and Embeddings
sections.summary: Demonstrates tokenization with examples showing subword splitting that doesn't always match human intuition (e.g., 'reinjury' splits into 'rain' and 'jury'). Shows embeddings tab where each token maps to 768 numbers starting at column 3 through column 770.

sections.title: Attention and Multi-Layer Perceptron Layers
sections.summary: Covers the 12 layers (blocks 0-11), each with attention and MLP. Attention lets tokens look backward at other tokens for context (e.g., 'he' looks at 'Mike', 'moves' disambiguates 'quick'). Shows attention head with causal masking (zeros above diagonal) and MLP using MMULT matrix multiplication and activation functions.

sections.title: Language Head and Forward Pass Completion
sections.summary: The language head reverses the embedding process: takes the last token's output, applies layer norm, multiplies by unembedding matrix to get logits, then picks highest probability token. At temperature zero, this is simply argmax; at higher temperatures, sampling algorithms like beam search are used.

sections.title: Residual Connections and Logit Lens MRI
sections.summary: Introduces residual connections as an information superhighway allowing information to skip layers. The logit lens technique inserts the language head between layers to observe intermediate predictions. For 'If today is Tuesday tomorrow is,' Wednesday appears early, disappears, then reemerges in later layers. Researchers found only 4 components needed for this task, illustrating circuits across layers.

sections.title: Transition to Brain Surgery
sections.summary: Brief transition from the MRI section to the brain surgery section, referencing Anthropic's pioneering work in this area.

sections.title: Brain Surgery: Sparse Autoencoders and Feature Steering
sections.summary: Covers Anthropic's work on scaling monosemanticity that produced Golden Gate Claude, a model obsessed with the Golden Gate Bridge. Sparse autoencoders decompose the residual stream into interpretable features that can be amplified or suppressed. Joseph Bloom, Neel Nanda, and others are building sparse autoencoder features for GPT-2 small; layer 2's feature 7650 corresponds to 'Jedi.' Anand demonstrates injecting this Jedi steering vector into the residual stream at the start of block 2, changing GPT-2's output from 'Mike pulls out his phone' to 'Mike pulls out his lightsaber.' Also mentions representation engineering (PCA-based) and activation steering (concept-minus-suppress vector) as alternative techniques.

sections.title: Closing: Architecture, Communication, and Resources
sections.summary: Anand concludes that understanding LLM internals helps engineers know their tools' behavior and limitations, follow latest research, and communicate clearly with non-technical stakeholders to dispel perceptions of magic. He notes model architecture affects prompting: RWKV recommends swapping instruction and context order because its pseudo-attention can't look backward like a regular transformer. References provided for all research discussed. The spreadsheet is downloadable at spreadsheets-are-all-you-need.ai, and a step-by-step course launched on Maven.
